Format: a frame for a fighter card on the battle screen of a dark fantasy mobile card battler. Landscape 5:4 canvas, seen straight on, flat, not in perspective, perfectly symmetric from left to right. The frame is a landscape rectangle, and its window — the empty opening where the game later puts the fighter's portrait — is a clean landscape rectangle with straight inner edges and small square corners, about 1.35 times as wide as it is tall; the window takes almost the whole frame. Everything on the canvas is solid pure black except the frame itself: the window is pure black and completely empty — no face, no figure, no glow, no smoke, no mist, no reflection, no pattern inside it.

Proportions, strictly: the two side bars and the bottom bar are thin plain bars, each about 3% of the frame width, with no ornament on them; nothing hangs below the bottom bar and nothing sticks out sideways from the lower two thirds of the frame. All ornament gathers on the top bar and at the two top corners: it rises above the top bar by at most one tenth of the frame width and reaches sideways past the side bars by at most one thirtieth of the frame width. Nothing hangs down into the window: the inner edge of the frame is a clean straight line on all four sides.

In the game it is seen very small, about 90 pixels wide: bold, simple, strong silhouettes and one clear accent rather than fine filigree; a thin crisp light rim runs along the inner edge of the frame so that the portrait separates from it. The enemy frames form a ladder of danger: the more dangerous the enemy, the heavier and more terrifying its frame — bone, thorns, horns, dark flame, glowing cracks of carst — awe and dread, never wealth or gloss.

The enemy rank: biome boss — the master of the deepest step of a biome; awe and dread. A heavy frame of blackened iron and old yellowed bone. Two thick curved horns of old bone grow from the top corners and sweep outward and up in low, wide curves; a row of short bone thorns runs along the top bar; at the top center a crown of bone thorns holds a narrow slit of burning ember light (#F0564A fading to #E6A84B), like a half-open watching eye; thin dark smoke curls from the horn tips and stays close to them. The bottom corners are heavy dark iron caps, flat.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the frame and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole frame with all its ornament fits inside the central 90% of the canvas: an empty black margin stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no interface elements other than the frame itself: no buttons, no bars, no gauges, no name plate, no label, no banner with lettering. No skulls, no blood, no gore. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine. Nothing at all inside the window.

Who he is: a scribe who wanted to read inside the dwarven mountain, where knowledge is gathered, not hidden. Subject: Bjorn Bedframe, a dwarf of the guild guard, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the gate of the dwarven mountain is narrow on purpose — it holds one war machine on its iron bed and one dwarf. For forty years that dwarf was he. The machine strikes while it has fuel, he stands while he can stand — that was how they shared the work. Right now the machine beside him has fired until it burnt out dry and fallen silent, and he holds the gap alone with his shield until the shift horn: to leave the post before the relief comes is a disgrace. Character: stolid, dutiful and unbreakable — a dwarf who counts in shifts; his teeth bared under the beard with the strain, his brows lowered, his eyes calm and fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide, once-broken nose; in his sixties, a black beard shot with grey in two thick braids bound with iron rings. Subject: Eldgrim Hammer, a dwarf smith of the guild guard, a warrior of great strength of the Earth school. Who he is: by day he forged the hinges for the gate of the dwarven mountain, and when beasts came up from the streams he took the same hammer and went to the gate: a thing you made yourself you defend yourself. The gate was closed, and he stayed on the other side. Right now he stands outside the gate and strikes. Character: calm, exact and unstoppable — a craftsman who works under blows as evenly as at his anvil; his brows lowered in concentration, his jaw clenched, his eyes narrowed on the target; he is not angry, he is working. Subject: Skeggi Firelock, an old dwarf gunner of the guild guard, a marksman of the Fire school. Who he is: a dwarven gun does not forgive haste — hurry, and the powder flashes in your face. In forty years he never once hurried, and the northerners of the caravans laughed that he aimed longer than they fought. At the gate they said: Skeggi shoots late, but only once. Right now he has one charge left and a beast comes straight at him; he has waited until it is so close that missing is impossible. Character: unhurried, calm as stone, with a dry, quiet humour; his face utterly still, one eye narrowed along the barrel, a faint dry calm in the corner of his mouth. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad weathered face with a wide nose; in his seventies, bushy grey brows and a magnificent long grey beard in one thick braid, tucked into his belt, away from the pan. Framing: a close portrait from the belt up — his head, his shoulders, his arms and the gun fill the picture; the bottom edge of the picture cuts him at the belt; his legs and boots are out of the picture. The long barrel runs toward the right edge, and the flash of the shot bursts at the right edge of the picture. Pose, the moment of the shot: the camera is low; he is rock-still, turned toward the right, the heavy gun levelled at his shoulder. He has exactly two arms: his near hand supports the long barrel from beneath; his far hand holds the stock tight to his shoulder, a finger on the trigger. The gun fires at point-blank range: scarlet fire of the Fire school and white smoke burst from the flared muzzle toward the right. Details that tell his story: (1) the gun: a long, heavy dwarven hand-cannon — an eight-sided barrel of dark iron bound with brass bands, a flared muzzle, a heavy carved wooden stock and a small brass pan by the breech; (2) the bandolier across his chest: every loop is empty; (3) the braided beard tucked into his belt; (4) a brass powder flask at his belt; (5) a smouldering slow-match coiled around his wrist. Place: a stony wasteland at night, a dark stream glinting behind him; far away, the torches of the gate of a lone dwarven mountain. Scarlet light of the Fire school from the muzzle and from embers drifting up from below; cold dark night around.

Subject: Nyal the Ore-Changer, a dwarf trader at the gate of the great dwarven mountain, a gatherer of wealth. Who he is: at the gate everything is exchanged for everything, and he exchanged ore for anything at all — as long as it was equal for equal. People offered him credit — cheap, long, recorded by their judges — and he refused them all: a dwarf recognizes neither debt nor gift. Once a season he checked his shelves against his book, and the book always tallied. Right now a stranger beyond the right edge makes an offer, and he names equal for equal. Character: shrewd, proud and incorruptible — a dwarf who has never owed anyone a thing; one bushy brow raised, a small satisfied smile in his beard, his eyes weighing the stranger. He is short and enormously broad: a barrel chest, a thick short neck, a broad face with a wide nose; in his sixties, a bald head and a long iron-grey beard in a single thick braid bound with copper rings. Pose, the moment of the deal: the camera is low; he leans over his counter toward the right. He has exactly two arms: his near hand is thrust out toward the right, palm up, holding out a heavy lump of raw ore glittering with veins of metal — his offer; his far hand rests flat on a thick closed ledger with an iron clasp. Between them on the counter stand great brass scales, their two pans perfectly level. Details that tell his story: (1) the great brass scales with both pans exactly level — equal for equal; (2) the ledger is closed with its iron clasp, nothing written visible; (3) shelves behind him crowded with goods from all over the world: bales of cloth, jars of oil, bundles of herbs, tools and blades; (4) a small leather pouch set apart at the edge of the counter — his apprentice's share, paid in advance; (5) a jeweller's loupe on a cord around his neck, a heavy leather coat with brass buttons. Place: a trading stall at the great gate of a lone dwarven mountain, where caravans come to exchange: lanterns, crates, pack animals and traders blurred in soft focus, the gate's massive stone arch above. Warm lantern light rises from the counter below and glints on the ore and the brass; the orange glow of the foundries deep inside the gate.

Art style: dark fantasy game UI art for a mobile RPG — gloomy, heavy, noble and uneasy. Hand-painted digital painting: visible confident brush strokes, simplified planes, deep near-black shadows, crisp rim light on the edges. A muted, desaturated palette: soot black (#050607, #121518), graphite (#262B31), blackened iron, old dark leather, dark bronze, yellowed bone, weathered stone. Everything is matte, worn and aged: no bright polished gold, no gloss, no shiny jewellery, no clean saturated game-UI colors. Light is scarce and precious: the frame is lit from below with a crisp rim light along its edges; only its magical parts glow from within. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon, no flat vector style.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no text in the reply.

Format: a frame for a fighter card on the battle screen of a dark fantasy mobile card battler. Landscape 5:4 canvas, seen straight on, flat, not in perspective, perfectly symmetric from left to right. The frame is a landscape rectangle, and its window — the empty opening where the game later puts the fighter's portrait — is a clean landscape rectangle with straight inner edges and small square corners, about 1.35 times as wide as it is tall; the window takes almost the whole frame. Everything on the canvas is solid pure black except the frame itself: the window is pure black and completely empty — no face, no figure, no glow, no smoke, no mist, no reflection, no pattern inside it.

Proportions, strictly: all four bars are equally slim — the top bar is as slim as the two side bars and the bottom bar, each about 3% of the frame width; the side bars and the bottom bar are plain, with no ornament on them; nothing hangs below the bottom bar and nothing sticks out sideways from the lower two thirds of the frame. All ornament stands on the top bar and at the two top corners: it rises above the top bar by at most one tenth of the frame width; horns and spikes at the top corners grow upward and only a little outward, reaching sideways past the side bars by at most one thirtieth of the frame width. Nothing hangs down into the window: the inner edge of the frame is a clean straight line on all four sides. No smoke, sparks, motes or particles anywhere around the frame.

In the game it is seen very small, about 90 pixels wide: bold, simple, strong silhouettes and one clear accent rather than fine filigree; a thin crisp light rim runs along the inner edge of the frame so that the portrait separates from it. The enemy frames form a ladder of danger: the more dangerous the enemy, the heavier and more terrifying its frame — bone, thorns, horns, dark flame, glowing cracks of carst — awe and dread, never wealth or gloss.

The enemy rank: rank-and-file — the lowest and weakest rank. The plainest frame of the set: a thin frame of dark worn iron with hairline cracks and a few small round rivets; small plain angular iron brackets at the four corners, flat and low; at the top center only a tiny plain iron clasp, barely raised above the top bar. Absolutely no horns, no thorns, no spikes, no claws and no crest anywhere: nothing rises above the top bar except the tiny clasp. No light of its own, only a faint cold rim light from below. Humble and grim.

The background is solid pure black (#000000), flat, edge to edge: no gradient, no texture, no floor, no cast shadow, no vignette, no checkerboard. Any glow stays close to the frame and fades into the black within a short distance. The whole frame with all its ornament fits inside the central 90% of the canvas: an empty black margin stays on every side — top, bottom, left and right.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no interface elements other than the frame itself: no buttons, no bars, no gauges, no name plate, no label, no banner with lettering. No skulls, no blood, no gore. No pentagrams, no occult signs, no crosses, no religious symbols. No bright polished gold, no glossy plastic shine. Nothing at all inside the window.

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close half-body portrait from the waist up. THE HERO LOOKS AT THE VIEWER: the body is turned slightly, three-quarters, but the head faces us and the eyes look straight into the camera, meeting the eyes of the person who looks at the picture — a living person with a story, not an illustration of an action. The face is the heart of the picture: large, in the upper third, sharply lit, with an expression that tells who they are. Give the face exactly the specific features described below — bone structure, eyes, nose, mouth, skin, scars, age — and nothing generic: this face must not look like any stock fantasy character. The pose is this hero's own signature gesture from their story, calm or tense as the story says — not a generic attack. Clothing and objects are specific to their life, worn and personal; the hero has a color palette of their own. The background is the place of their story, with depth, darker and softer than the figure. Light from below and from the story's own light sources; rim light separates the figure from the background. The lower edge sinks gradually into shadow — no band, no plate, nothing written.

Subject: Grimsa the Horn, an old dwarf woman who for sixty years sounded the shift horn of Stone-Heim, the dwarven city inside a mountain, and was never once late. In the mountain the horn replaces the sun: three voices — shift, meal, shift — and by her horn the city worked, was born and died. In battle she is a controller of the Earth school: the voice of her horn stops and binds. The moment: her last shift. She has just sounded the horn for the last time and sat down at its lever, and she breathes slowly, counting, the way she taught every young miner — 'Breathe like Haldur', after the miner who breathed and counted for five days under a rockfall and lived. She is not afraid: proud, stern and at peace. She looks straight at you as if you were the young one about to go down to the lower drifts, and she is telling you: breathe, and don't be late. Her face — make it hers alone: very old but hard as a hearthstone; a broad, square dwarven face, weathered and ruddy from sixty years of hot steam; deep-set, very pale grey eyes, almost silver, clear and sharp, under heavy lids and thick straight iron-grey brows; a strong bumpy nose that was broken once and set a little crooked; a wide thin mouth pressed tight, with deep vertical lines above the upper lip from a lifetime of blowing and counting breaths; a net of fine wrinkles darkened with old soot; a pale, smooth, shiny old burn scar across her left cheek from a steam jet; heavy earlobes stretched by thick brass rings. No beard — a dwarf woman with a strong jaw. Hair: thick iron-grey hair braided into a heavy crown wound around her head, held with small brass pins. She is half deaf from sixty years beside the horn: a small dented brass ear-trumpet hangs on a cord at her chest. Her clothing: a heavy, faded oxblood-red wool coat of the horn-keepers, patched at the elbows, its brass buttons rubbed dull; over it a scorched leather apron; thick grey knitted cuffs; on a thong around her neck three tiny brass whistles of different lengths — shift, meal, shift. Her hands are big and knotted, with swollen knuckles and a pale band of callus across the palm. Pose and gesture: she sits on a worn iron stool beside the great lever of the horn, half-turned toward us. Her near hand rests on the lever's handle, polished to bright metal by sixty years of her grip; her other hand lies flat on her chest, feeling her breath; her lips are just parted in the middle of a count; her eyes meet ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the lever handle is worn bright where her hand holds it, with a long row of small plain notches filed into the dark iron below — one for each year, simple cuts, no letters or symbols; (2) the horn itself above and behind her: three great brass pipes of different lengths fed by a thick steam pipe, a last wisp of steam still curling from their mouths; (3) a small round window of the horn booth behind her looks out over the dark hollow of the mountain city — tiers of forges and furnace glow far below; (4) a tin mug on a shelf, soot on the walls. Light: the amber-orange light of the Earth school rises from the furnaces far below the window and from thin cracks in the stone floor, lighting her face from below; warm glints on brass; the cool silver of her eyes against the warm light.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no glyphs, no writing on paper, books, maps or stones, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no name plate, no dark band at the bottom, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood, no monsters in the picture. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes. No generic fantasy face; the hero does not look away — the eyes look into the camera.

Subject: Grimsa the Horn, an old dwarf woman who for sixty years sounded the shift horn of Stone-Heim, the dwarven city inside a mountain, and was never once late. In the mountain the horn replaces the sun: three voices — shift, meal, shift — and by her horn the city worked, was born and died. In battle she is a controller of the Earth school: the voice of her horn stops and binds. Who she is, right now: her last shift. She hauls down the great lever of the horn for the last time, and the horn roars over the city. Even now she counts her breath, the way she taught every young miner going down to the lower drifts: 'Breathe like Haldur', after the miner who breathed and counted for five days under a rockfall and lived. Character, written in her body: stern, proud, unshakeable, dry and caring at once — her jaw set, her back straight as a pillar despite her age, her brows drawn down, her pale eyes fixed on you as if you were the young one about to go down, telling you without words: breathe, and don't be late. Her face — make it hers alone: very old but hard as a hearthstone; a broad square dwarven face, weathered and flushed from sixty years of hot steam; deep-set, very pale grey eyes, almost silver, clear and sharp, under heavy lids and thick straight iron-grey brows; a strong bumpy nose, once broken and set a little crooked; a wide thin mouth, lips just parted mid-count, with deep vertical lines above the upper lip from a lifetime of counting breaths; fine wrinkles darkened with old soot; a pale smooth old burn scar across her left cheek from a steam jet; heavy earlobes stretched by thick brass rings. No beard — a dwarf woman: short, very broad and sturdy, with strong forearms. Hair: thick iron-grey hair braided into a heavy crown around her head, held with small brass pins. Her clothing, her own palette of oxblood red and brass: a heavy faded oxblood-red wool coat of the horn-keepers, patched at the elbows, brass buttons rubbed dull; a scorched leather apron over it; thick grey knitted cuffs; on a thong around her neck three small brass whistles of different lengths — shift, meal, shift; a small dented brass ear-trumpet on a cord at her chest, for she is half deaf from sixty years beside the horn. Pose, the moment of the last horn: she stands at the great iron lever, which rises almost to her shoulder; she has exactly two arms: her near hand grips the lever's handle — polished bright by sixty years of her grip — and hauls it down with her whole weight; her far hand is pressed flat on her chest, feeling her breath. Her body leans into the lever, but her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the lever's handle is worn to bright metal, with a long row of small plain notches filed into the dark iron below it — one for each year, simple cuts, no letters or symbols; (2) above and behind her the horn itself: three great brass pipes of different lengths, fed by a thick steam pipe, blasting steam into the air; (3) rings of amber-orange light and dust ripple outward from the pipes' mouths — the Earth school voice of the horn that stops and binds; (4) far behind her, through the open front of the horn tower, the dark hollow of the mountain city — tiers of forges and furnace glow far below. Place and light: the horn tower high above the underground city of Stone-Heim; amber-orange Earth light rises from the furnaces below and from cracks in the stone floor and lights her face from below; warm glints on brass; the cool silver of her eyes against the warm light; steam and dust in the air.

Subject: Anselm the Ninth, a human scribe from Laiten-Gard, the harbour city in the west, and a mage of the Water school. Who he is: he wanted to read inside the dwarven mountain, where knowledge is gathered, not hidden. Nine times he carried knowledge to the gate of the mountain's Library — lists of laws, maps, recipes, poems — and nine times the gatekeeper said: 'We already have that.' Then he sat down by the gate and wrote down, from the refusals alone, like reading footprints, everything the mountain already knew — an inventory the dwarves themselves did not have. On the tenth time they let him in. The moment: the tenth time. He stands before the great gate, holding out his hard-won inventory, and the small door in the gate is finally opening for him. Character, written in his body: patient, stubborn, dry, quietly triumphant — a man who waited nine refusals and never raised his voice; his chin lifted a little, a thin tight smile that he cannot hold back, his eyes on you as if to say: 'the tenth time'. His face — make it his alone: about forty-five; a narrow, gaunt, long face with sharp cheekbones and hollow cheeks from the days spent sitting by the gate; clean-shaven with a day's dark stubble; large dark-brown, short-sighted eyes, a deep squint line between the brows; a long thin nose with a reddened dent on the bridge from years of reading lenses, which now hang on a cord at his chest; thin lips with a small blue-black ink stain on the lower lip where he wets his quill; straight black hair cut in a blunt fringe across the forehead, grey at the temples. His hands: long thin fingers stained with ink up to the second knuckle, a writer's callus on the middle finger. His clothing, his own palette of deep sea-blue and ink-black with pale salt-stains: a travel-worn scribe's long coat of deep sea-blue wool from the west, its hem crusted with pale salt from the harbour road; narrow sleeves; many pockets stuffed with rolled lists and folded maps; a brass inkwell hanging from his belt, its ink glowing with a deep blue light; a cord at his belt with nine knots tied in it — one knot for every refusal. Pose, standing, the moment of the tenth time: he stands upright before the gate, body turned three-quarters toward the door; he has exactly two arms: his near arm holds against his chest a thick, hand-bound ledger with a worn leather cover, closed, bristling with slips of paper — his inventory of what the mountain knows; his far hand is raised palm up, and from his inkwell a ribbon of dark water rises and coils around his fingers into a slow glowing spiral — the Water school, ink turned to living water, with no letters in it. His head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) the cord with nine knots at his belt; (2) the ledger bristling with slips, its cover worn pale where his thumb holds it; (3) the reading lenses on a cord; (4) behind him the great plain stone gate of the dwarven mountain — enormous, closed — and in it a small iron-bound door just opening for the first time, warm lamplight spilling out through the gap onto the step. Place and light: the gate of the mountain Library at dusk; cool blue Water-school light from the glowing spiral lights his face from below; warm lamplight from the opening door behind him; a thin mist of spray around his hand; dust and droplets in the light.

Subject: Bastian Olt, a human hunter from the western lands, a fighter of the Air school who kills with speed and precision. Who he is: the Keeper of the Showcases of the mountain Library hired him for one season to take the Grey One, a great grey she-beast, alive, for the Library's upper hall; the contract says only: Grey. Alive. He had taken bigger beasts. After a season he extended the contract at his own expense: the Grey One led him in circles over the stones and every time turned up behind his back, watching. He understood that she was studying him too. The moment: the last time. Stones are coming down the mountainside; he stands with his net on his shoulder, and high on a ledge behind him the Grey One has come, looked down at him, and is about to leave. He never closed the contract. Character, written in his body: a proud professional who has just realized he is the one being watched: a crooked, rueful half-smile, one eyebrow raised, weight easy on his back foot, a hunter's alert stillness; he looks straight at you as if to share the joke: I was the prey all along. His face, make it his alone: about thirty-eight; a long, lean, sun-browned face with a long jaw; narrow light green-hazel eyes creased at the corners from squinting into wind; a thin white scar cutting through his left eyebrow; the tip of his right ear missing, torn off long ago by a beast; a straight nose peeling from sunburn; a wide mouth with one chipped front tooth; ash-blond hair, short and wind-tangled; a short copper-blond stubble; a scatter of freckles across his nose. His clothing, his own palette of moss green, weathered brown leather and grey: a patched moss-green hunter's jerkin over a laced leather shirt, sleeves rolled to the elbow; lean forearms roped with muscle and crossed with old claw scars; a necklace of big claws and fangs, trophies of bigger beasts; a rolled contract tied with a faded ribbon tucked into his belt, no visible writing; a hunting knife at his hip. Pose, standing, the moment the Grey One watches him: he stands turned three-quarters, the heavy rolled hunting net slung over his near shoulder, held there by his near hand; he has exactly two arms: his far hand holds a short, light hunting spear low at his side, point down, relaxed; wind of the Air school streams around him in pale green-white ribbons, lifting his hair and the loose ends of the net; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) a single long tuft of grey fur caught in the mesh of the net, the only thing he ever took from her; (2) behind him and above, on a high ledge of dark stone, the Grey One: a huge long-limbed grey beast like a lynx, calm, only her silhouette and two pale eyes looking down at him, half hidden in mist; (3) small stones and dust tumbling down the slope behind him; (4) the claw necklace and the rolled contract. Place and light: a steep grey scree slope of the mountain at dusk, mist between the stones; pale green-white light of the Air school swirls around him and lights his face from below; a cold sky glow behind the ridge.

Subject: Bjorn Bedframe, a dwarf of the guild guard, a defender of the Earth school. Who he is: the gate of Karoksorr is narrow on purpose: it holds one war machine on its iron bed and one dwarf. For forty years that dwarf was he. The machine strikes while it has fuel; he stands while he can stand; that is how they shared the work. The moment: his last shift. Beasts that long ago stopped being beasts came up from the streams to the gate; the machine beside him fired until it burnt out dry and fell silent; he stepped into the gap and held it with his shield until the horn, because to leave the post before the relief comes is a disgrace. Now the horn has sounded and his relief has come on time: he still stands in the gap, shield up, and turns his face to you, as if you were the relief, with the look of a dwarf handing over his gate: you are on time, now it is yours. Character, written in his body: stolid, dutiful, unbreakable and bone-tired; his feet planted wide, his shoulders squared behind the shield, his jaw still clenched, but his eyes calm and approving. His face, make it his alone: an old dwarf, weathered as the gate stone; a broad, heavy, square face; a nose flattened and broken more than once, bent to one side; a drooping left eyelid from an old blow; small, deep-set, very dark eyes under one heavy ridge of brow; the outer half of his left ear missing; skin streaked with soot and sweat; a thick black beard shot with grey, gathered into one massive braid bound by three iron rings; the sides of his head shaved, a black-and-grey crest of hair on top. Short, enormously broad, a barrel chest, a thick short neck. His clothing, his own palette of iron grey, deep ochre and soot black: a heavy coat of overlapping iron scales over thick leather, the scales scratched and scorched; a deep ochre guild tabard, torn and singed at the hem; broad iron pauldrons; iron vambraces; a leather cap bound with iron bands. Pose, standing, the moment of handing over the gate: he stands square in the narrow gap between plain rough stone walls, body turned three-quarters; he has exactly two arms: his near arm holds up a tall, heavy rectangular shield of riveted iron, dented and patched with plates over forty years, braced but lowering a little now; his far hand rests on the iron bed-frame of the silent war machine beside him, like a hand on an old comrade's shoulder; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell his story: (1) the war machine beside him: a squat dwarven engine of blackened iron and brass on a massive riveted iron bed-frame, a short thick barrel still glowing dull red, a thin curl of smoke, burnt out and silent; (2) the shield: dents, scorch marks, patch plates riveted over patch plates, forty years at the gate; (3) deep claw scratches across the face of the shield from the last night; (4) the gateway: a narrow passage of rough, plain dark stone blocks with no carving, room only for the machine and one dwarf, heavy iron doors deep behind him. Place and light: the narrow gate of a lone dwarven mountain at the end of the night; amber-orange Earth-school light rising from cracks in the stone floor lights his face from below; the dull red glow of the spent machine on his armour; smoke and stone dust in the air.

Subject: Trud the Tincture-Keeper, a dwarf woman, a healer of the mines, with no elemental school: her light is the light of the elven tinctures and her lamp. Who she is: the elves bring tinctures into the mountain, for burns, broken bones and poisoning, and she knew which one heals what, and gave the miners one per shift; more than one only at the alarm horn. In forty years the alarm sounded three times. The third time she went down to the rockfall with a full box and gave them out without counting, for the first time in her life. The bad air below takes the healer too, and the box emptied more slowly than she did. The moment: she holds out the last flask, to the boy who pushes the ore carts; his shift is just beginning, and hers is over. She holds it out to you, as if you were that boy. Character, written in her body: stern, practical, warm underneath, and utterly spent: her breath short in the bad air, sweat on her brow, but her hand holding the flask is steady and her gaze is firm: take it, and go. Her face, make it hers alone: a dwarf woman of middle age for her people; a round, full face with ruddy weathered cheeks gone pale now; small, keen hazel eyes with deep crow's-feet from squinting at labels by lamplight; a short snub nose; a gap between her front teeth; a dark mole on her right cheek; a smear of soot across her forehead; her lips tinged a faint sickly yellow by the bad air; chestnut hair gone salt-and-pepper, in two short thick braids tucked under a mustard-yellow kerchief knotted at the nape. No beard: a dwarf woman, short, broad and strong-armed. Her clothing, her own palette of mustard yellow, dark brown and glass green: a dark brown work dress with sleeves rolled up; a heavy leather apron covered in small loops and pockets for vials, most of them empty now; a cloth breathing-mask pulled down around her neck; a small brass lamp hanging at her belt. Pose, standing, the moment of the last flask: she stands in the collapsed drift, body turned three-quarters; she has exactly two arms: her near arm holds against her hip an open wooden tincture box packed with straw, only empty slots left; her far hand holds out toward us, toward the viewer, the last small elven glass flask, glowing a soft green; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the open box of straw with empty slots where the flasks were; (2) the empty vial loops of her apron; (3) the breathing-mask around her neck: she gave hers away too; (4) behind her the rockfall in the drift: broken timber props and fallen stone, a thick yellow haze of bad air hanging low. Subject: Frida Ore-Dust, a dwarf woman, an ore sorter of the upper yard, a controller of the Earth school who blinds and chokes her enemies. Who she is: for forty years she sorted ore at the long tables of the upper yard and knew by the colour of its dust which ore would give metal and which would eat the lungs. Once, beasts came up from the streams to the road while the caravan stood unloaded; she slit a sack of the most vicious dust and let it fly at them with the wind; the beasts went blind and choked before the guard could even unsling their guns. The dust she knew knew her too: forty years at the sorting table do not pass for nothing. In her last shift she breathed slowly, counting, and finished sorting her box to the end, because badly done work is sacrilege. The moment: the slit sack on her shoulder is still pouring; a long river of rust-red dust streams away from her on the wind; she lifts a pinch of the dust between thumb and finger and lets it trickle, reading its colour, and looks straight at you with a dry, knowing look: I know exactly what this dust does. Character, written in her body: sharp, dry, fearless and quietly dying of her trade: her back straight, her chin up, a slight rasp in her breath, a thin satisfied smile. Her face, make it hers alone: an elderly dwarf woman; a long, narrow face with a sharp chin, unlike most dwarves; dark amber-brown eyes narrowed and very keen; thick eyebrows dusted rust-red; a long pointed nose with a raw, reddened tip from the dust; thin lips; greyish skin with rust-coloured dust ground into every crease and wrinkle; cheeks flecked with ore stains like freckles; white-grey hair cropped short and standing up stiff with dust; a pair of small round dust-goggles with brass rims pushed up on her forehead; a thin cloth mask pulled down under her chin. No beard. Her clothing, her own palette of rust red, ochre and slate grey: a canvas smock caked with ore dust, leather sleeves, fingerless leather gloves stained in many colours; a sorter's belt hung with small glass sample jars of different coloured dusts: ochre, black, green, blood-red. Pose, standing: she stands turned three-quarters; she has exactly two arms: her far hand holds the slit sack over her shoulder by its neck, the dust pouring from the slit and streaming away on the wind behind her; her near hand is raised before her chest, a pinch of dust trickling from her gloved fingers and glowing in the light; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Details that tell her story: (1) the goggles and the mask she never has time to put on; (2) the belt of coloured sample jars; (3) behind her the upper sorting yard: long stone sorting tables heaped with ore sorted by colour, a waiting ore caravan with carts and mules; (4) the road going down toward the streams at dusk, veiled by the rust-red cloud. Place and light: the upper yard of a dwarven mountain at dusk, wind blowing; amber-orange Earth-school light rises from ore crystals on the tables and from cracks in the paving, lighting her face from below; the streaming dust glows rust-red in the light.

Subject: Vigdis Rubble, a young dwarf woman, a mage of the Earth school who strikes with a storm of stones. Who she is: on her poor lower ledge the stone obeyed her earlier than the pick, and the guild wrote her down as an Earth mage, one of those who chose the strange, as the dwarves say. The locks of the workshops went to more important mages; she walked with the guild guard to the gate, and where the gunners ran out of charges, her rubble began. The guild gave her no stone to cast with, so she cast with herself: the guild counts its charges, but nobody but she counted her years. The moment: the last sortie. The charges have run out for everyone at once; she raises from the slope everything that lies on it and gives her last year without bargaining, because when the price is named, a dwarf does not bargain. Character, written in her body: proud, poor, fierce and at peace with the cost: her feet planted, her jaw set, her eyes blazing. No beard. Short, broad, strong. Her clothing, her own palette of charcoal black, undyed grey-brown wool and amber light: a patched guild-issue coat far too big for her, its sleeves rolled up; a rough undyed wool tunic; a plain iron guild token on a cord at her neck; a miner's pick slung across her back. Pose, standing, the moment of the last spell: she stands on the slope, body turned three-quarters; she has exactly two arms, both lowered and spread wide, palms turned up, fingers open, lifting; around her, stones, rubble and gravel from the whole slope rise into the air in a slow storm, glowing at their cracks; her braids float; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Subject: Eldgrim Hammer, a dwarf smith of the guild guard, a fighter of the Earth school who crushes with raw strength. Who he is: by day he forged the hinges for the gate; when the beasts came up from the streams, he took the same hammer and went to the gate, because a thing you made yourself, you defend yourself. Subject: Nyal Ore-Changer, an old dwarf trader of the gate, a gatherer of goods with no elemental school. Who he is: at the gate everything is traded for everything, and he traded ore for anything at all, as long as it was equal for equal. Once a season he checked his shelves against his book, and the book always balanced. In his last shift he felt the clock in his chest slowing and stood at his counter to count it all once more: not a single line against him in anyone's book, not one against others in his. To his young helper he paid his share a shift in advance; that is not a debt, it is a trade: the helper will work it off without him. The moment: he sets the helper's share on the counter and slides it toward you, as if you were that helper, and looks straight at you with grave, fair dignity: not a debt, a trade. Character, written in his body: precise, honest to the grain, proud and calm: upright, unhurried, every movement exact. His face, make it his alone: an old dwarf; a round face with high prominent cheekbones; small, shrewd, dark eyes under neat white brows; a sharp hawk nose; thin precise lips under a neatly trimmed white moustache; a bald head with a ring of white hair; a white beard carefully combed and divided into two short square forks, each bound with a copper bead; a heavy brass earring shaped like a tiny pair of scales in one ear; a jeweller's loupe hanging on a fine chain at his chest. His clothing, his own palette of bottle green, copper and cream: an old but well-kept bottle-green merchant's coat with copper buttons; a cream linen shirt; a leather money belt with many small pouches. Pose, standing, the moment of the last trade: he stands behind his stone trading counter, body turned three-quarters; he has exactly two arms: his near hand pushes a small tied leather pouch of coin across the counter toward us; his far hand rests on a lump of raw ore on the counter beside the scales; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. No beard. Short and sturdy. Her hands: small, with shiny pale wax burns on the fingertips. Her clothing, her own palette of dark grey wool, candle gold and pale wax white: a long dark grey wool robe with a hood-veil; a belt hung with bundles of thin candles and a small brass snuffer; a leather satchel of fresh candles. Pose, standing, the moment of the leaning flame: she stands turned three-quarters in the hall; she has exactly two arms: her near hand holds up a tall thick candle in a brass holder at chest height, its flame bending strangely downward; her far hand is raised, palm open toward the niches, with a soft warm amber light of healing around her fingers; her head is turned to us and her eyes look straight into ours. Place and light: the deepest hall of a dwarven mountain, vast and dark, rows of niches with small candles; the candlelight and soft amber Earth-school light from the cracks light her face from below; still air, a few motes of dust drifting down.

Subject: Nazir the Ashen, a human fire mage of the College, who sees off the dead of Endalor. Who he is: he came to Endalor at the call of the Temple of Fire and saw off the dead from the edge of the city's disc: in Endalor they burn everyone who bears the mark of a resident, and it is the cleanest work in the city. When the deep hall of the dwarven mountain burned out, the dwarves for the first time called a fire mage, to teach their own to keep fire at the niches. He taught for a year and left without thanks: dwarves thank by trade, and he had nothing to trade. He died at home, at the edge, and asked his apprentice to wait for the wind. His face, make it his alone: about sixty; dark brown skin; a lean, long, ascetic face with a high forehead and hollow cheeks; deep-set dark eyes with long lashes, grey with fine ash; grey eyebrows; a thin, closely trimmed white-grey beard; a shaved head with a smudge of grey ash across the forehead, the mark of his work; laughter lines at the corners of his eyes; old small burn scars on the backs of his hands. His clothing, his own palette of ash grey, charcoal and ember orange: a long ash-grey College robe with a charcoal-dark stole, its hem singed; a narrow ember-orange sash; a small brass censer hanging from his belt, trailing a thin line of smoke; simple leather sandals, not visible. Pose, standing, the moment of the wind: he stands at the edge, body turned three-quarters toward the open sky; he has exactly two arms: both hands are held before him at chest height, cupped and opening, and grey ash with tiny glowing embers lifts from his palms and streams away on the wind; a small calm flame of the Fire school burns in the hollow of his near palm; his head is turned to us and his eyes look straight into ours. BOOK 5: a grimoire — blackened riveted iron with short sharp spikes at its top and bottom corners, carved yellowed bone along it, and warm amber light (#E6A84B) glowing from the thin edges of the pages at the top of the spine.

Промт, как он ушёл в модель
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: a sheet of square ability icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the picture in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top: one clear central image with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below in the color of the magic school; crisp rim light on the edges of the forms; a few sparks and dust motes in the light. All icons share the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one set, and each icon differs clearly from its neighbours in shape and composition.

The magic school of this sheet is Fire: scarlet fire (#F0564A) with orange and amber flames, glowing embers, grey ash and soot-black stone; the light from below is scarlet and amber. Attacking spells burn a violent, jagged scarlet. Supporting spells — healing, warmth, shields and strength for allies — glow a softer warm gold and amber with rounded, calm shapes. A spell for all targets shows something wide that fills its cell; a spell for two or three targets shows two or three of its thing; a spell for one target shows one focused object. Attacks move to the right, toward the enemies.

The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 icons.

Row 1: a towering wave of scarlet fire rolling to the right across the ground, filling the whole width, its crest curling over like a breaking sea wave; a bright white-hot spark leaping to the right in a jagged chain of three arcs, a small burst of flame where each arc lands; a funeral pyre of stacked dark logs erupting into one huge column of scarlet flame, sparks spiralling upward; two cupped hands at the bottom releasing a wide, soft fan of warm golden breath full of glowing motes; three small soft golden flames rising like young sprouts from one bed of embers; a dagger blade glowing orange-hot, pressed flat against a strip of white linen bandage, a small puff of steam rising.

Row 2: a huge translucent dome of warm amber flame arched over the dark ground like a protective vault; a circular wall of warm amber flames standing on the stone floor, seen from slightly above, a protective ring around a calm empty centre; a heavy round iron shield wreathed in amber flame, sparks bursting off its rim where a blow has just struck it; a wide low front of creeping scarlet fire spreading across dry grass and ash, many small flames side by side from edge to edge; a flaming torch flying in an arc to the right, trailing fire and dripping burning pitch that lights three small fires below; a charred log burning from within, deep cracks glowing scarlet, three tongues of flame rising from it.

Row 3: a small campfire in a ring of stones seen from the side, its warm golden glow spreading around in soft rings, a few sparks drifting up; three smouldering golden coals nestled in soft grey ash, each with a gentle warm glow and tiny rising motes; a small stone hearth with an iron cooking pot hanging over a steady golden fire, warm light spilling out; thick choking black smoke billowing across the whole cell, scarlet embers smouldering inside it; two dense columns of grey smoke rising from smouldering coals and twisting together into a screen; a single blinding flash of white-hot flame bursting from one point, sharp radiant rays, the centre almost white.

Row 4: grey ash falling like heavy snow over the whole cell, every flake glowing scarlet at its edge; two simple flame-shaped marks smeared in glowing ash on a dark stone surface, as if drawn with a finger; a red-hot branding iron with a simple flame-shaped head glowing scarlet, smoke curling from it; a wide iron brazier with five tall flames rising side by side and leaning together, scarlet and gold, sparks rushing upward; two crossed battle axes whose blades glow orange-hot, flames running along their edges; one sword standing upright, its blade glowing white-hot from hilt to tip, heat shimmer around it.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.

Format: a sheet of square ability icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the picture in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top: one clear central image with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below in the color of the magic school; crisp rim light on the edges of the forms; a few sparks and dust motes in the light. All icons share the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one set, and each icon differs clearly from its neighbours in shape and composition.

The magic school of this sheet is Fire: scarlet fire (#F0564A) with orange and amber flames, glowing embers, grey ash and soot-black stone; the light from below is scarlet and amber. Attacking spells burn a violent, jagged scarlet. Supporting spells — healing, warmth, shields and strength for allies — glow a softer warm gold and amber with rounded, calm shapes.

The grid: exactly 4 columns and 4 rows, 16 icons. Rows 1 and 2 are ultimate spells — the grandest, most epic images of the set, bigger in scale, with bright gold highlights in the fire. Row 3 are passive traits — calm, emblem-like single objects, no action. Row 4 are reactions — an instant answer to an event in battle, shown as one moment of action.

Row 1: a colossal pillar of scarlet and white fire striking down from above onto a single point, the ground cracking and turning to ash around it; a great phoenix of golden fire with its wings spread wide, rising upward and showering warm golden sparks; a huge dome of fire covered by a lattice of glowing golden lines, flames lashing outward from its surface; an enormous wildfire engulfing everything from edge to edge, towering flames and black smoke in a red glow, sparks everywhere.

Row 2: an ancient massive stone hearth with an eternal golden flame, warm light flooding outward, golden embers floating; a giant swirling vortex of black smoke with glowing embers caught inside it, like a dark storm; a massive round iron seal with a plain face slamming down into a thick layer of ash, a ring of glowing ash exploding outward from under it; a raised armoured fist wrapped in roaring scarlet flame and golden sparks.

Row 3: a trail of smouldering footprints glowing in ash, every third footprint bursting into a small flame; a single drop of blood glowing like molten metal, a tiny flame burning inside it; a leather blacksmith's bellows blowing into a bed of coals, the flames flaring up bright; a lump of coal shaped like a heart, glowing golden from within through its cracks.

Row 4: an enemy blade striking an iron gauntlet, a burst of flame blasting back along the blade toward the attacker; a heavy critical strike — a blade biting deep into dark leather armour, the cut bursting into scarlet flame; a flame leaping in an arc from a falling, dying torch to an unlit torch, setting it ablaze; a fallen warrior's dented helmet lying in ash, the ash rising from it in a column of glowing sparks and flame.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: a sheet of square ability icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the picture in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top: one clear central image with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below in the color of the magic school; crisp rim light on the edges of the forms; a few sparks and dust motes in the light. All icons share the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one set, and each icon differs clearly from its neighbours in shape and composition.

The magic school of this sheet is Earth: amber-orange Rubidium crystals (#EB9D40) glowing from within cracks in dark brown and grey rock, ochre dust, gnarled roots and warm clay; poison is a thick sickly mustard-yellow venom; the light from below is amber-orange. Attacking spells are heavy, jagged and crushing — dark rock split by glowing amber cracks. Supporting spells — healing, living sap, shields and strength for allies — glow a softer warm gold and honey-amber with rounded, calm shapes. A spell for all targets shows something wide that fills its cell; a spell for two or three targets shows two or three of its thing; a spell for one target shows one focused object. Attacks move to the right, toward the enemies. Every icon, even the widest, is built around one clear central object with a bold silhouette — never only smoke, dust, snow, fog or a scattered pattern.

The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 icons.

Row 1: a massive rockfall — a cliff breaking apart and a torrent of dark boulders tumbling down to the right across the whole width, amber light glowing in the cracks of the falling rocks; a round boulder bursting apart in mid-air into three big jagged shards of amber-veined rock that fly to the right; a single huge stone spike erupting from cracked ground and thrusting up and to the right, glowing amber magma in its cracks; an old tree stump cut flat, its rings welling up with glowing golden sap that overflows and spreads across the ground in soft streams; three smooth round cakes of red-brown healing clay on a flat stone, soft golden light seeping from their cracks; a large geode split open into two halves, its hollow heart lined with amber crystals shining warm gold.

Row 2: a wide curved wall of massive standing stones rising from the ground across the whole cell, warm amber light glowing between the stones; three tall rough slabs of stone standing side by side like shields, each edged with warm amber light; one lone tall crag of dark rock standing firm like a tower shield, a warm golden glow along its edge; a big puffball mushroom in the center bursting open and releasing a wide cloud of sickly mustard-yellow spores that spreads over the whole cell; three tall thorns of dark stone growing from the ground in a cluster, thick yellow venom dripping down them into small puddles; the head of a viper with scales like stone, rearing and striking to the right, its fangs bared and dripping yellow venom.

Row 3: a great gnarled root arching across the whole cell like a bridge, many drops of glowing golden dew hanging from it; three young curling roots rising from dark soil, each holding a glowing golden bud; one thick drop of glowing golden resin sliding down the rough bark of a dark pine trunk; an ancient stone cauldron in the center overflowing with heavy mustard-yellow fog that rolls out across the ground over the whole cell; two thick roots bursting out of the cracked ground and twisting into tight coils like snares; one armoured leg sunk up to the knee in a pillar of solid rock that has grown up around it and grips it fast.

Row 4: a row of five dark iron shields standing edge to edge across the whole cell, all cracked and crumbling, grey dust pouring from the cracks; two dark iron shields, each split in half by a jagged crack, amber light glowing in the cracks; one dark iron breastplate crumbling into sand and pebbles from its edges; a range of dark mountain peaks filling the whole width, their tops glowing warm gold under a soft golden sky; two heavy helmets hewn from grey granite, warm golden light glowing in their seams; one bare forearm covered in overlapping plates of stone like scales, warm golden light in the seams between the plates.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.

Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top: one clear central image with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below in the color of the magic school; crisp rim light on the edges of the forms; a few sparks and dust motes in the light. All icons share the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one set, and each icon differs clearly from its neighbours in shape and composition.

The magic school of this sheet is Light: pale gold and white light (#F4E6AE), bright white rays, warm cream-gold, polished silver and white stone; the light from below is pale gold and white. Attacking spells are harsh and blinding — hard white beams and sharp jagged rays. Supporting spells — healing, radiance, shields and consecration for allies — glow a softer warm gold with rounded, calm shapes and soft halos. Every icon, even the widest, is built around one clear central object with a bold silhouette — never only smoke, dust, snow, fog or a scattered pattern.

The grid: exactly 4 columns and 4 rows, 16 icons. Rows 1 and 2 are ultimate spells — the grandest, most epic images of the set, bigger in scale, with bright gold highlights in the white light. Row 3 are passive traits — calm, emblem-like single objects, no action. Row 4 are reactions — an instant answer to an event in battle, shown as one moment of action.

Row 1: colossal pillars of white light crashing down from the sky across the whole cell, the ground shattering where they land; a great golden tree of light bursting into bloom from a dead stump; a colossal vault of the heavens — a huge arch of golden stars over the dark ground; a sea of tall white-gold flames engulfing the ground across the whole cell.

Row 2: a vast break in dark clouds with countless golden rays pouring down onto the land; a gigantic blazing white sun at its highest point, so bright that everything below is washed out in white; a great bell of white gold ringing, waves of harsh white light cracking dark masks around it; a magnificent suit of white-gold plate armour standing empty like a monument, radiating golden light.

Row 3: one golden halo floating in the dark, a soft ring of light; one perfectly clear crystal sphere on a small silver stand, pure light inside it; one white-gold spear standing upright, calm; one candle flame standing perfectly straight while a gust of wind bends around it.

Row 4: a shield of golden light appearing in front of a warrior just as a heavy blow lands on it; a cup overflowing with golden light, the spilled light hardening into a glowing golden rim around it; a fallen warrior's sword stuck in the ground, a column of warm golden light rising from it and spreading; a raised polished silver shield flashing a blinding white glare back at a huge descending enemy blade.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.

Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Format: a sheet of square spirit-talisman icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the talisman in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top. A spirit talisman is a small keepsake that holds a trait of someone else's soul — how that soul struck, guarded or survived — and gives the trait to the one who wears it. Every cell shows exactly one talisman at rest, seen straight on: it hangs straight down in the middle of the cell from a short loop of knotted dark cord that comes down from the top edge of the cell. The talisman is a small flat charm of dark materials — dark forged iron, dark carved bone, dark wood, dark leather or dark stone — shaped as the thing named for its cell, with fittings of worn old gold. Every talisman without exception has one smooth oval cabochon of milky moonstone set in it, clearly visible; inside the moonstone a captured soul-trait turns like a small ghostly wisp of coloured light, and one thin ghostly wisp of the same light curls up from the charm like breath on a cold night. The charm and its cord fill about two thirds of the cell with one bold, simple silhouette that stays readable at 48 px. Behind it: a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks, a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell, and a soft, dim glow of pale ghostly light behind the charm that fades smoothly into the dark stone — never a flat disc or a plate. Light rises gently from below; crisp rim light on the edges of the charm; a few dust motes in the light. Painted exactly like the ability icons of this game: loose, confident painterly brush strokes, soft painted edges and deep shadows — no black outlines, no flat sticker look. No action, no spell effects, no scenes: always one still object. All talismans share the same cord, the same moonstone, the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one family, and each differs clearly from its neighbours in the shape of its charm.

All talismans of this sheet are combat talismans — traits of how a soul struck and endured; their soul-light, in the moonstone and in the ghostly wisp, is a fierce ember red-orange (#E8603C) like a smouldering coal — never pink.

The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 talismans. For each cell, the shape of its charm:

Row 1: a small crimson-lacquered cup with a single drop of blood on its rim; a stone spring-head with two thin trickles of water flowing from one source; a long icicle of pale frosted crystal; an iron fist clenched around a broken chain link; an almond-shaped eye of dark bronze, the moonstone as its pupil; a black clawed hand with long curled fingers.

Row 2: a small flame carved from grey ash-stone; a curved dancer's blade bent into a graceful spiral; a small hooded cloak of dark cloth, its folds held by a gold clasp; a long curved scythe blade; a round flat stone worn smooth by ages, one deep old footprint of a bare foot pressed into it, moss in its cracks; a heart of dark granite with seams of gold.

Row 3: a thin silver crescent with three small pale teardrops hanging from it; a small iron helmet visor with a thin needle passing through its eye slit; an arrowhead with a single drop of blood at its tip; a long bone needle threaded with a pale thread that is unravelling; a big stone-eater's fang with chips of stone stuck in its grooves; a moth with ashen, singed wings.

Row 4: a round bronze hunter's tag with a notch cut into its edge and a small ring target carved on it; a heavy plumb weight of dull grey lead; a thick drop of dark amber resin with a tiny insect trapped inside; a long crimson thorn on a piece of dark stem; a small wooden yoke dusted with grey ash; a proud wolf's head carved from dark bone.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.

This sheet holds two kinds of talismans. Rows 1 and 2 are seal talismans — traits of refusal, of a soul that would not let a curse take hold; their soul-light is a cold turquoise (#48E5D4). Every seal talisman has the same shape: a square plaque of dark stone standing on one corner like a diamond, with a thick bevelled rim of old gold; the moonstone is set in its top corner, and the middle of the plaque bears one bold, simple emblem in raised old gold, named for its cell — a picture, never a letter or a sign of writing. Rows 3 and 4 are collector's signs — loot talismans, the keepsakes of a gatherer who always found what others missed; their soul-light is a warm lucky gold (#F0CC4F). Every collector's sign has the same shape: a round token of dark wood with an old-gold rim, the moonstone set at its top, and across the face of the token one small real thing is bound with thin cord, named for its cell.

Row 1: the emblem: a running hare; the emblem: a feather; the emblem: an open hand; the emblem: a knotted bandage; the emblem: a footprint half wiped away; the emblem: a needle and thread sewing a seam.

Row 2: the emblem: a smooth seamless breastplate; the emblem: an open eye; the emblem: a pair of closed lips; the emblem: an owl; the emblem: a cord with a row of knots; the emblem: a heart with a small flame inside it.

Row 3: the thing bound to the token: a bent iron nail; the thing bound to the token: a small brown mushroom; the thing bound to the token: a short wooden plank; the thing bound to the token: a lump of rusty brown iron ore; the thing bound to the token: a coil of dried sinew; the thing bound to the token: a tiny clay dish of grey ash.

Row 4: the thing bound to the token: a tiny glass vial of yellow acid; the thing bound to the token: a curved fang; the thing bound to the token: a hooked claw; the thing bound to the token: a folded piece of tanned leather; the thing bound to the token: a small bone; the thing bound to the token: a tiny clay pot of red dye.

Промт, как он ушёл в модель
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: a sheet of square spirit-talisman icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the talisman in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top. A spirit talisman is a small keepsake that holds a trait of someone else's soul — how that soul struck, guarded or survived — and gives the trait to the one who wears it. Every cell shows exactly one talisman at rest, seen straight on: it hangs straight down in the middle of the cell from a short loop of knotted dark cord that comes down from the top edge of the cell. The talisman is a small flat charm of dark materials — dark forged iron, dark carved bone, dark wood, dark leather or dark stone — shaped as the thing named for its cell, with fittings of worn old gold. Every talisman without exception has one smooth oval cabochon of milky moonstone set in it, clearly visible; inside the moonstone a captured soul-trait turns like a small ghostly wisp of coloured light, and one thin ghostly wisp of the same light curls up from the charm like breath on a cold night. The charm and its cord fill about two thirds of the cell with one bold, simple silhouette that stays readable at 48 px. Behind it: a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks, a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell, and a soft, dim glow of pale ghostly light behind the charm that fades smoothly into the dark stone — never a flat disc or a plate. Light rises gently from below; crisp rim light on the edges of the charm; a few dust motes in the light. Painted exactly like the ability icons of this game: loose, confident painterly brush strokes, soft painted edges and deep shadows — no black outlines, no flat sticker look. No action, no spell effects, no scenes: always one still object. All talismans share the same cord, the same moonstone, the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one family, and each differs clearly from its neighbours in the shape of its charm.

All talismans of this sheet are hunting talismans — traits of a tracker who learned how an enemy lives and dies; their soul-light is a cold pale silver-blue moonlight (#BFD8F0). A scourge talisman is sharp: its trophy is pierced by an iron spike. A ward talisman is round: its trophy is set in the middle of a small round shield-shaped charm.

The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 talismans. For each cell, the shape of its charm:

Row 1: a broken bronze gear tooth pierced by a short iron spike; a plain smooth black stone pierced by a short iron spike; a shard of a cracked clay face-mask pierced by a short iron spike; a big hooked beast claw pierced by a short iron spike; a shard of dull violet crystal in a small iron cage, pierced by a short iron spike; a small bleached bone bound along a short iron spike with red thread.

Row 2: a glass bead holding a trapped spark of pale energy, pierced by a short iron spike; a tiny cracked hourglass pierced by a short iron spike; a small round shield-shaped charm with a broken bronze gear tooth set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a plain smooth black stone set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a shard of a cracked clay face-mask set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a big hooked beast claw set in its middle.

Row 3: a small round shield-shaped charm with a shard of dull violet crystal in a tiny iron cage set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a small bleached bone set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a glass bead holding a trapped spark of pale energy set in its middle; a small round shield-shaped charm with a tiny whole hourglass set in its middle; a torn horsehair plume from a war-chief's helmet, bound with cord; a huge fang of a great beast.

Row 4: a small hand sickle; a round bronze wheel with plain notches around its rim and no numerals; a small triangular war pennant of plain cloth on a spear tip; a small bone flute; a tiny leather diary with a clasp and a pressed feather sticking out of it; a small broken golden crown.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.
Боевые (11), «талисман скрыт», добыча (9), охотничьи (2) и запасная клетка — сеткой 6×4

This sheet holds three kinds of talismans; the soul-light, in the moonstone and in the ghostly wisp, follows the kind named for each row: combat talismans — fierce ember red-orange (#E8603C); loot talismans — warm lucky gold (#F0CC4F); hunting talismans — cold pale silver-blue moonlight (#BFD8F0). The grid: exactly 6 columns and 4 rows, 24 talismans. For each cell, the shape of its charm:

Row 1: a small shield with a torn scrap of banner cloth tied to it; a scorpion's curled stinger; a small balance scales of old gold; a small black cat carved from dark wood, curled up, its eyes half closed; a boar's tusk bound with red cord; one feather quill whose tip glows.

Row 2: two feather quills crossed and tied together; a tiny hourglass with a single glowing grain of sand left in it; a dwarven war hammer with a heavy square head; a pair of heavy iron shackles, closed; a small ivory mask of a calm sleeping face with closed eyes; a talisman hidden in mist, in neutral pale grey light instead of ember red: only the dark outline of a charm on its cord, veiled by thick pale grey mist so that its shape cannot be seen.

Row 3: a small nugget of raw gold dusted with gold; a tiny stoppered glass vessel with a turquoise swirl inside; a small lantern with a pale blue flame inside; a magpie feather with a small shiny gem tied to it; a small bronze censer with a curl of smoke; a small bulging sack tied with cord.

Row 4: an old coin with a hole in its middle; a small knotted net with a pale blue flame caught in it; a small sheaf of wheat bound with gold; a small hunting bow with a tuft of grey wool tied to its string; a spiral seashell; a small smooth mask of grey stone with no face at all, blank and featureless.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. The moonstone on it is small — no bigger than a fingernail — and sits at the very top of the disc, just under the cord. The middle of the disc belongs to the thing named for the cell: it is large, centered, covering about half of the disc, and lashed flat across the wood with a few turns of thin cord — it is the main subject of the icon and never hangs on its own.
