Row 3: the thing lashed to the token: a small ball of yarn; the thing lashed to the token: a pinch of softly glowing pale dust on a leaf; the thing lashed to the token: a flake of grey stone with straight carved grooves, crumbling into dust; the thing lashed to the token: a short stub of a candle; the thing lashed to the token: an empty little glass vial; the thing lashed to the token: a bent iron bracket.

Row 4: the thing lashed to the token: a small lump of scrap-metal ingot; the thing lashed to the token: a drop of amber resin; the thing lashed to the token: a lump of black coal; the thing lashed to the token: a tiny bottle of black ink; the thing lashed to the token: a small bronze gear; the thing lashed to the token: a rolled piece of raw hide with fur.

Промт, как он ушёл в модель
Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.

Format: a sheet of square equipment icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the item in every row are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top. Every cell shows one piece of equipment, empty and standing alone — nobody wears or holds it — centered, about two thirds of the cell, seen straight on or in a clear three-quarter view, with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below; crisp rim light on the edges of the item; a few dust motes in the light. Painted exactly like the ability icons of this game: loose, confident painterly brush strokes, soft painted edges and deep shadows — no black outlines, no flat sticker look. No ornaments that look like letters, runes or writing. Each row is one kind of item shown in seven rarities, from left to right, and the item grows richer with every step — in material, in fittings and in the light inside it — while its kind, its view and its basic silhouette stay the same, so the row reads as one item growing in rarity:
1. common — plain, worn dark iron and scuffed leather, no ornament, no gems, no inner light; cold pale white light (#E6E8EA) from below.
2. rare — sound polished steel with brass rivets and a thin edging of gold; one small yellow gem (#F0CC4F) glows faintly; warm yellow light from below.
3. unique — fine blued steel with thin silver inlay; one turquoise gem (#1FB8D0) glows softly; turquoise light from below.
4. epic — dark steel with gold filigree edging and a violet crystal (#A986EE) glowing from within; thin violet light seeps from its seams; violet light from below.
5. ancient — heavy ancient metal darkened by ages, with gold fittings; a red crystal (#E85A4E) with a swirl of flame inside it; thin red cracks glow from within; red light from below.
6. primordial — black metal and old gold of a primordial make; bright orange fire (#EB9D40) burns inside its crystal and seams like molten metal; orange light from below.
7. timeless — the richest of all: dark metal and bright gold with ornate fittings; a large green crystal (#5FD67A) radiating light; green energy glows from within every seam; green light from below.
All items share the same brushwork, lighting and level of detail, so they read as one set.

The grid: exactly 7 columns and 3 rows, 21 icons. The columns are the seven rarities, from common on the left to timeless on the right.

Row 1 — leg armour: a pair of plate leggings seen straight on, standing upright like a pair of trousers joined at a belt, two legs side by side with a narrow gap, ending above the ankles — no boots; the common one is plain leather with iron knee caps, the higher ones gain full plates, gold rims and glowing crystals on the knees.

Row 2 — boots: a pair of heavy boots standing side by side in a three-quarter view, toes pointing to the lower right; the common one is worn leather with iron toe caps, the higher ones gain plates, gold buckles, spurs and glowing crystals at the ankles.

Row 3 — a weapon: a longsword set diagonally, its hilt at the lower left and its point at the upper right; the common one is a plain iron blade with a leather grip, the higher ones gain a finer blade, an ornate gold crossguard, a pommel crystal and light along the groove of the blade.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.
Шлем, доспех, перчатки — по семь редкостей, сеткой 7×3

Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top. Every cell shows one piece of equipment, empty and standing alone — nobody wears or holds it — centered, about two thirds of the cell, seen straight on or in a clear three-quarter view, with a bold silhouette that stays readable at 48 px, on a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks and a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell. Light rises from below; crisp rim light on the edges of the item; a few dust motes in the light. Painted exactly like the ability icons of this game: loose, confident painterly brush strokes, soft painted edges and deep shadows — no black outlines, no flat sticker look. No ornaments that look like letters, runes or writing. Each row is one kind of item shown in seven rarities, from left to right, and the item grows richer with every step — in material, in fittings and in the light inside it — while its kind, its view and its basic silhouette stay the same, so the row reads as one item growing in rarity:
1. common — plain, worn dark iron and scuffed leather, no ornament, no gems, no inner light; cold pale white light (#E6E8EA) from below.
2. rare — sound polished steel with brass rivets and a thin edging of gold; one small yellow gem (#F0CC4F) glows faintly; warm yellow light from below.
3. unique — fine blued steel with thin silver inlay; one turquoise gem (#1FB8D0) glows softly; turquoise light from below.
4. epic — dark steel with gold filigree edging and a violet crystal (#A986EE) glowing from within; thin violet light seeps from its seams; violet light from below.
5. ancient — heavy ancient metal darkened by ages, with gold fittings; a red crystal (#E85A4E) with a swirl of flame inside it; thin red cracks glow from within; red light from below.
6. primordial — black metal and old gold of a primordial make; bright orange fire (#EB9D40) burns inside its crystal and seams like molten metal; orange light from below.
7. timeless — the richest of all: dark metal and bright gold with ornate fittings; a large green crystal (#5FD67A) radiating light; green energy glows from within every seam; green light from below.
All items share the same brushwork, lighting and level of detail, so they read as one set.

The grid: exactly 7 columns and 3 rows, 21 icons. The columns are the seven rarities, from common on the left to timeless on the right.

Row 1 — a shield: a round shield seen straight on, with a raised boss in the middle; the common one is weathered wooden planks with a dark iron rim, the higher ones gain metal facing, gold rims, ornament and a glowing crystal as the boss.

Row 2 — a ring: a heavy ring standing upright in a three-quarter view, so that both its thick round band and its top are clearly visible, the hole of the band open; the common one is a plain iron band with a dull grey stone, the higher ones gain silver and gold, filigree and a larger glowing crystal of their colour.

Row 3 — an amulet: an oval pendant hanging on a short chain that rises to a loop at the top; the common one is a plain iron disc on a leather cord, the higher ones gain silver and gold settings, filigree and a larger glowing crystal of their colour.

No text, no letters, no numbers, no captions, titles or labels under, over or inside the icons, no real-world alphabets, no runes or marks that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no frames or borders drawn inside the cells. No pentagrams, no occult signs. No magenta or pink anywhere inside the icons: magenta appears only in the gutters.

Format: a sheet of square spirit-talisman icons for a mobile RPG, painted together as one consistent set. The icons stand in a precise grid of equal square cells; the number of columns and rows and the talisman in every cell are listed below, row by row from the top, each row from left to right. Between the cells run narrow straight gutters of flat, uniform pure magenta (#FF00FF), and the same magenta gutter runs around the outside of the whole grid. All gutters have the same width, all cells have the same size, and nothing crosses a gutter. Every cell is its own complete square painting filled from edge to edge — the game puts its own frame on top. A spirit talisman is a small keepsake that holds a trait of someone else's soul — how that soul struck, guarded or survived — and gives the trait to the one who wears it. Every cell shows exactly one talisman at rest, seen straight on: it hangs straight down in the middle of the cell from a short loop of knotted dark cord that comes down from the top edge of the cell. The talisman is a small flat charm of dark materials — dark forged iron, dark carved bone, dark wood, dark leather or dark stone — shaped as the thing named for its cell, with fittings of worn old gold. Every talisman without exception has one smooth oval cabochon of milky moonstone set in it, clearly visible; inside the moonstone a captured soul-trait turns like a small ghostly wisp of coloured light, and one thin ghostly wisp of the same light curls up from the charm like breath on a cold night. The charm and its cord fill about two thirds of the cell with one bold, simple silhouette that stays readable at 48 px. Behind it: a dark near-black stone background with faint cracks, a darker vignette toward the edges of the cell, and a soft, dim glow of pale ghostly light behind the charm that fades smoothly into the dark stone — never a flat disc or a plate. Light rises gently from below; crisp rim light on the edges of the charm; a few dust motes in the light. Painted exactly like the ability icons of this game: loose, confident painterly brush strokes, soft painted edges and deep shadows — no black outlines, no flat sticker look. No action, no spell effects, no scenes: always one still object. All talismans share the same cord, the same moonstone, the same brushwork, lighting, level of detail and palette, so they read as one family, and each differs clearly from its neighbours in the shape of its charm.

This sheet holds four talismans of different kinds; the soul-light, in the moonstone and in the ghostly wisp, follows the kind named for each cell, and each cell keeps strictly to its own colours.

The grid: exactly 2 columns and 2 rows, 4 talismans. For each cell:

Row 1: a talisman hidden from view, in neutral pale grey light instead of a coloured soul-light: the knotted cord comes down into thick swirling pale grey mist that wraps the charm completely, only a vague dark shape of a charm shows through — no face, no mask, nothing recognisable; a seal talisman, cold turquoise soul-light: a square plaque of dark stone standing on one corner like a diamond, with a thick bevelled rim of old gold, the moonstone set in its top corner; in the middle of the plaque one bold emblem in raised old gold — a strip of linen cloth tied in a simple knot, no cross, no plaster.

Row 2: a hunting talisman, cold pale silver-blue soul-light: a small horned helmet of dark iron with one of its horns broken off, the moonstone set in its brow; a collector's sign, warm lucky gold soul-light: a round flat disc of dark wood with a thick old-gold rim hanging from the cord, a small moonstone at the very top of the disc; lashed flat across the middle of the disc with a few turns of thin cord, large and centered, a broken bronze lever from an old mechanism — a short flat bar with a round hole at one end and a pin through it, not a wrench.
